stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: SpaceX declares Starship ready for orbit, sets launch date next week
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: SpaceX has declared its Starship vehicle is ready for orbital flight.
The company has scheduled the next launch for the upcoming week.
Achieving orbit is noted as a major milestone for the Starship program.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The pipeline associated with the model is 'text-generation', indicating its primary function.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed to run locally on user hardware, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed improvement based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost translates to higher quality model outputs and faster response times.
The optimization also results in reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution into the agent system.

stories.title: The Roman telescope has enough gas for 22 years, double NASA's expectations
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The Roman Space Telescope is pioneering in-space refueling technology.
The current fuel supply is projected to last for 22 years, exceeding initial NASA estimates.
This capability marks a significant advancement in long-duration space missions.

stories.title: Agility’s new humanoid robot will stop, squat to avoid harming human coworkers
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Agility is developing a new humanoid robot designed for collaborative human workspaces.
The robot incorporates advanced safety features, such as stopping and squatting to prevent harm to coworkers.
This development signals a move toward robots operating outside traditional physical safety cages.

stories.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive workspace for scientific research leveraging AI agents.
Features a core mechanism of 'recursive-in-recursive self-improvement' combining harness evolution and RL.
Agents continuously improve by transforming researcher feedback and execution evidence into learning tasks.

stories.title: PhysStream: Streaming Physics-Grounded Video Generation with Structured Scene Memory and Fine-Grained Motion Control
stories.author: Lingjie Liu
bullet_points: Introduces PhysStream, a new autoregressive model for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis.
Addresses limitations in current controllable video generation by moving beyond coarse prompts to fine-grained, physically meaningful manipulation.
Incorporates structured scene memory and aims to control dynamics based on physical principles rather than just pixel-space signals.

stories.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
stories.author: Ali Şenol
bullet_points: Introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework to improve LLM reliability.
CoSQ makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of the required factual support.
Evaluated across multiple model families on the TruthfulQA dataset to control for LLM hallucination/weak support.

stories.title: JustFit: 200K-Token LLM Serving on a 24 GiB Laptop with Just-in-Time State Management
stories.author: Yuhua Chen
bullet_points: Introduces JustFit, an MLX-based inference runtime designed to run large LLMs (200K tokens) on constrained hardware like a 24 GiB laptop.
Achieves memory efficiency through novel techniques including KVExec for compressed KV execution, PhaseSwap for component residency, and StateTrans for state-preserving serving.
The system manages state and materialization just-in-time, offering performance improvements independent of standard model-weight quantization.

stories.title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceBuddy, an interactive workspace designed to integrate continually improving scientific agents into researcher workflows.
Features a core mechanism of 'recursive-in-recursive self-improvement,' combining harness evolution with model reinforcement learning.
The system learns continuously by transforming researcher requests, feedback, and execution evidence into learning tasks and evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
stories.author: Ali Şenol
bullet_points: Introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only framework designed to improve LLM reliability.
CoSQ makes answer commitment conditional on an explicit assessment of the required factual information, addressing LLM hallucination.
Evaluated across multiple open-weight and hosted model families using the TruthfulQA dataset to test risk control.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services (Claude) with local, open-weight models (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving functionality on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Meta is reportedly ready to launch less pervy smart glasses
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly developing a new line of smart glasses codenamed 'Luna'.
The key differentiator for these new glasses is the complete absence of a camera.
This development appears to be a strategic response to public scrutiny over the video recording features of Meta's existing smart glasses.

stories.title: The EOS R8 Mark II is Canon’s lightest full-frame camera with stabilization
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Canon has released the EOS R8 Mark II, the second generation of the R8 camera.
The new model features a retro-inspired redesign and the addition of in-body image stabilization (IBIS).
The R8 Mark II aims to be a lighter, more accessible alternative to higher-tier models like the Canon R6 Mark II.

stories.title: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: New poll data indicates significant public unpopularity regarding AI and data center construction.
61% of likely voters surveyed oppose the building of data centers necessary to power AI technology.
The findings align with existing trends and are influencing political responses.

stories.title: Microsoft announces Windows and Surface event for October 7th
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is hosting a major Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7th.
The event is positioned to outline the future direction of Windows and Surface devices.
A key focus of the announcement will be the impact of local AI on the next generation of computing.

stories.title: Boston dumps Flock, says it shared data nationwide in violation of contract
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: Boston city government is taking action against Flock, a technology provider.
The core issue is that Flock allegedly enabled 'nationwide lookup' capabilities.
This action reportedly violates the terms of the contract signed with the city.

stories.title: Demand for EV chargers is outstripping supply, says ChargePoint report
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Demand for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is currently exceeding available supply.
The report highlights that EV adoption is continuing to grow, even within the US market.
The shortage points to a critical bottleneck in supporting the increasing number of EVs.

stories.title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
stories.author: Ratul Mahajan
bullet_points: The paper addresses 'agentic societies,' defined as autonomous AI agents coordinating across different principals with potentially misaligned goals.
Experimental results indicate that even honest and competent agents struggle to achieve satisfactory outcomes with current communication and control mechanisms.
The research highlights vulnerabilities where faulty or malicious agents can disrupt collaboration or pursue harmful objectives.

stories.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs
stories.author: Shinji Watanabe
bullet_points: LACE introduces a novel Layer-Wise Compression (LACE) method for dynamic frame rate codecs.
The research addresses the high computational cost associated with high frame rates in neural audio codecs used in speech language modeling.
LACE improves upon prior methods by applying compression across multiple quantization layers, unlike previous single-step or single-codebook approaches.

stories.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
stories.author: Muhamad Risqi U. Saputra
bullet_points: The paper introduces ENCP, an Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction method specifically for Vision-Language-Navigation (VLN) models.
Uncertainty estimation is highlighted as a critical need in VLN to ensure agents make safer and more reliable navigation decisions.
Standard Conformal Prediction fails in sequential VLN tasks, necessitating the proposed episode-normalized approach to maintain coverage guarantees.

stories.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
stories.author: Amir Feder
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty of evaluating social reasoning in LLM assistants due to subjective user narratives and lack of ground truth for social properties.
Introduces 'Fuse,' a novel multi-agent simulation framework specifically designed for studying user-mediated social reasoning.
Focuses on improving the reliability and evaluation methods for LLM assistants used in social consultation settings.

stories.title: Det-LIME: Detector-Aware, Multi-Instance Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection
stories.author: Brinnae Bent
bullet_points: Introduces Det-LIME, a new explainability method designed specifically for object detection tasks.
Addresses a gap in marine mammal research where existing explainability tools fail because they ignore multiple instances (social organisms/colonies) and produce single-instance outputs.
Focuses on integrating model interpretability into practical conservation workflows using black-box object detectors.

stories.title: ENCP: Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction for Vision-and-Language Navigation
stories.author: Muhamad Risqi U. Saputra
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for uncertainty estimation in Vision-Language-Navigation (VLN) models to ensure safer decision-making.
It proposes ENCP (Episode-Normalized Conformal Prediction) as an advanced framework to improve uncertainty estimation in VLN.
The work highlights a limitation of standard conformal prediction in sequential tasks like VLN, which the new method aims to resolve.

stories.title: FreqSpaNet: Frequency and Spatial Learning of SFPF for Physical Layer Hardware Integrity Detection
stories.author: Yuying Bian
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of hardware integrity verification where physical changes don't alter logical identity.
Introduces FreqSpaNet, a network designed to learn representations from Spatio-Frequency Polarization Fingerprints (SFPFs).
Focuses on open-set hardware anomaly detection by handling the distinct structural dependencies of frequency and spatial dimensions.

stories.title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
stories.author: David Simchi-Levi
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of transferring systematic bias from a large teacher LLM to a smaller student model during distillation.
Proposes 'Coupled Calibration and Learning' (CCL) to mitigate teacher bias, especially under covariate shift.
Offers a solution for LLM distillation scenarios where target-domain reward feedback is unavailable.

stories.title: Tables Decoded: DELTA for Structure, TARQA for Understanding
stories.author: Ganesh Ramakrishnan
bullet_points: The research addresses the core problem of table understanding in document intelligence, covering reconstruction and TabVQA.
It proposes an alternative to current Vision-Language Model (VLM) approaches that rely on table images.
The new method utilizes structured textual representations, which are argued to be more scalable and better aligned with LLMs.

stories.title: OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run
stories.author: Harry Grieve
bullet_points: Identifies a critical reproducibility problem in open-source language model training.
The issue stems from the non-associativity of floating-point arithmetic, even when using deterministic framework modes.
The research highlights that determinism is often lost when moving between different hardware environments.

stories.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
stories.author: Usman Aleem
bullet_points: The research investigates how pruning affects the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) specifically for context-grounded tool calling in smart homes.
The study compares degradation across diverse LLM architectures, including dense Transformers, dense hybrids, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
It systematically evaluates various pruning methods (depth, width, hybrid, expert) and measures the impact after supervised fine-tuning (SFT).

stories.title: LACE: Layer-Wise Compression for Dynamic Frame Rate Codecs
stories.author: Shinji Watanabe
bullet_points: LACE proposes a novel Layer-Wise Compression (LACE) method for dynamic frame rate codecs.
The research addresses the high computational cost associated with high frame rates in neural audio codecs used in speech modeling.
LACE improves upon prior methods by applying compression across multiple quantization layers, unlike single-step or single-codebook approaches.

stories.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
stories.author: Amir Feder
bullet_points: Addresses the difficulty of evaluating social reasoning in LLM assistants due to subjective user narratives.
Proposes 'Fuse,' a multi-agent simulation framework specifically designed for studying user-mediated social reasoning.
Focuses on the challenge of verifying social properties, such as inferring others' intentions, which lack ground truth.

stories.title: Enhancing Accessibility of Medical Texts through Large Language Model-Driven Plain Language Adaptation
stories.author: Hsin-Hsi Chen
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate Plain Language Adaptation (PLA) for medical texts.
PLA aims to simplify complex healthcare jargon to improve patient reading comprehension and accessibility.
The work leverages LLMs (like GPT and BART) for PLA, particularly in scenarios with limited task-specific data (zero/few-shot learning).

stories.title: Large Language Models Develop Belief State Geometry In-Context
stories.author: Xavier Poncini
bullet_points: The research investigates the internal representations within Large Language Models (LLMs) that enable In-Context Learning (ICL).
The study uses Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to provide structured data to LLMs, allowing researchers to probe for the model's 'belief state' (posterior distribution over hidden states).
This work offers deeper insight into how LLMs might implicitly model underlying probabilistic structures, moving beyond simple next-token prediction.

stories.title: ECHO: A Matched-Contrast Benchmark for Context-Sensitive Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Dialogue
stories.author: Yang Song
bullet_points: Introduces ECHO, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating context-sensitive turn-taking in full-duplex dialogue systems.
Addresses a limitation in existing benchmarks by pairing overlapping transcripts with contrasting multi-turn dialogue contexts.
Focuses on the critical distinction between interruptions requiring a floor yield and permissible backchannels in spoken conversation.

stories.title: Mistral X Mozilla: Private, Multilingual AI Browsing
stories.author: vertigoruntime
bullet_points: Collaboration between Mistral AI and Mozilla on AI browsing technology.
The resulting product focuses on private and multilingual AI browsing capabilities.
This suggests a trend toward privacy-focused, advanced AI integration in web browsing.

stories.title: AI Wrote Half My Codebase. The Maintenance Bill Showed Up in Month Three.
stories.author: debashish_ghosal
bullet_points: The article discusses the initial appeal of using AI for rapid code generation.
It highlights a critical, often overlooked, long-term cost associated with AI-generated code (maintenance).
The narrative suggests that initial cost savings from AI drafting are offset by future operational expenses.

stories.title: AI Generated Tests Are Passing And Still Lying To You
stories.author: thebitforge
bullet_points: The article discusses the deceptive nature of AI-generated tests.
It highlights a scenario where tests pass but the underlying feature is flawed.
This points to potential issues in modern software testing practices involving AI.
